attempted_claim: Let S be the extraspecial group of order 7^3 and exponent 7 (7^{1+2}_+), and let F be the Ruiz-Viruel exotic saturated fusion system on S with |Out_F(S)| = 48 (the D_16 x C_3 case). Let X be the unique minimal characteristic S-S-biset for F (Park 2011, Theorem 5.2) with e(X) = |X|/|S| = 134448, let G = Aut(_1 X) ≅ S wr Sigma_{e(X)} be Park's finite group with F = F_S(G) (S ≤ G not Sylow), and let H = < N_G(V) | V ≤ S F-essential > be the subgroup generated by the normalizers of the F-essential subgroups (Park 2011, Theorem 6.4). With S identified with its image in H and S ≤ S_0(H) in Syl_7(H), decide: does F_S(H) = F hold (as fusion among subgroups of S, without assuming S Sylow), and is d(H) = log_7 |S_0(H) : S| strictly smaller than Park's upper bound e(F) ≤ 425744 — i.e. does the Alperin-Goldschmidt-generated subgroup H already give a strictly smaller finite realization of the exotic F?
decisive_failure: Park's paper (arXiv:1011.4505) was read in full and its numerics verified computationally, but the explicit Out_F(S) action on essentials and the base-group projections of the N_G(V_i) needed to decide F_S(H)=F and the strict defect inequality were not recovered; the candidate iff reduction was refuted on its converse during decision-phase review, leaving no Audit-passing emergent result.
